hanuman_chalisa_1_6.original_text:
श्रीगुरु चरन सरोज रज निज मनु मुकुरु सुधारि।
बरनउँ रघुबर बिमल जसु जो दायकु फल चारि॥
बुद्धिहीन तनु जानिके सुमिरौं पवन-कुमार।
बल बुद्धि बिद्या देहु मोहिं हरहु कलेस बिकार॥
जय हनुमान ज्ञान गुन सागर। जय कपीस तिहुँ लोक उजागर॥
राम दूत अतुलित बल धामा। अंजनि-पुत्र पवनसुत नामा॥
hanuman_chalisa_1_6.transliteration:
Shree Guru charana saroja raja, nija manu mukuru sudhaari |
Baranaun Raghubara bimala jasu, jo daayaku phala chaari ||
Buddhihina tanu jaanike, sumiraun Pavana-Kumaar |
Bala buddhi bidyaa dehu mohin, harahu kalesa bikaar ||
Jaya Hanumaana gyaana guna saagara | Jaya Kapeesa tihun loka ujaagara ||
Raama doota atulita bala dhaamaa | Anjani-putra Pavanasuta naamaa ||
hanuman_chalisa_1_6.word_meanings: man-mukuru: mirror of the mind; sudhaari: cleansing; bimala jasu: spotless glory; kalesa: inner mental afflictions/sorrows; bikaar: psychological distortions/impurities; gyaana guna saagara: ocean of wisdom and virtues.
hanuman_chalisa_1_6.translation: Cleansing the mirror of my mind with the dust of the lotus feet of the Guru, I describe the spotless glory of Sri Rama, which bestows the four fruits of life (Dharma, Artha, Kama, Moksha). Knowing this body-mind to be limited in intellect, I remember the Son of the Wind—grant me strength, discerning wisdom, and true knowledge, and remove my inner afflictions and mental distortions. Victory to Hanuman, the ocean of wisdom and virtue, illuminator of the three worlds, messenger of Rama, abode of incomparable strength, son of Anjani and the Wind-God.

mahabharata_yaksha_prashna.reference: Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Aranyaka Parva), Yaksha Prashna
mahabharata_yaksha_prashna.original_text:
किमाश्चर्यं परं ब्रूहि?
अहन्यहनि भूतानि गच्छन्तीह यमालयम्।
शेषाः स्थावरमिच्छन्ति किमाश्चर्यमतः परम्॥
mahabharata_yaksha_prashna.transliteration:
Kim aashcharyam param broohi?
Ahany-ahani bhootaani gacchanteeha Yamaalayam |
Sheshaah sthaavaram icchanti kim aashcharyam atah param ||
mahabharata_yaksha_prashna.word_meanings: ahani-ahani: day after day; bhootaani: living beings; gacchanti: depart to; Yamaalayam: the abode of death; sheshaah: those who remain behind; sthaavaram icchanti: desire/assume permanent immortality; kim aashcharyam atah param: what greater wonder can there be than this?
mahabharata_yaksha_prashna.translation: The Yaksha asked: 'What is the greatest wonder in the world?' Yudhishthira replied: 'Day after day, countless beings depart to the abode of Death, yet those who remain behind act as though they will live here forever. What can be a greater wonder than this?'
